normal_signature: Smooth, glistening mucosal surface with pink to salmon-pink coloration
Visible vascular patterns (submucosal vessels) appearing as fine, branching red lines
Intact tissue continuity without breaks, ulcers, or raised masses
Presence of physiological folds, rugae, or sphincter structures (e.g., Z-line, pylorus)
Clean lumen free of excessive blood, pus, or foreign debris
hypothesized_anomaly_modes: Mucosal erosion or ulceration: Breaks in the epithelial layer exposing deeper tissue, often appearing as white/yellow slough or red craters.
Neoplastic growth: Abnormal tissue proliferation manifesting as polyps, nodules, or irregular masses protruding into the lumen.
Active hemorrhage: Presence of fresh red blood or clots indicating bleeding from the mucosal surface.
Inflammatory exudate: Accumulation of pus, fibrin, or thick mucus obscuring the normal vascular pattern and surface texture.
rules: if the image shows a distinct break in the mucosal surface with a crater-like appearance or white/yellow slough then lean anomaly
if the image shows a distinct raised mass, polyp, or irregular nodule protruding from the wall then lean anomaly
if the image shows active bleeding, fresh red blood, or dark clots then lean anomaly
if the image shows a smooth, continuous surface with visible vascular patterns and no raised lesions then lean normal
if the image shows physiological folds or sphincter structures with intact, glistening tissue then lean normal
if the image shows a clean lumen with only normal mucus reflections and no foreign debris then lean normal
